name: Lorenz attractor
description:
Lorenz's 1963 model of convection, dx/dt = σ(y − x), dy/dt = x(ρ − z) − y and dz/dt = xy − βz, with his σ = 10, ρ = 28 and β = 8/3: the system that made chaos famous. The solution never settles and never repeats. x swings irregularly between −18 and 20 as the state circles one lobe of the butterfly-shaped attractor and then the other, while z rises and falls between about 1 and 48. x and y go negative, so "cannot go negative" is off on all three.

Chaos means that any difference grows about tenfold every two and a half seconds, a solver's own errors included. Run the model with dp45, vern7 and the NDF solver at the same tight tolerance (1e-10): they agree to four figures at t = 20, have parted by t = 28, and by the end are unrelated, with x(50) at 6.32, 4.99 and −0.81. Each is as good an answer as the others to a question whose answer cannot be known that far ahead.
